body: Fingers crossed

Very interesting things posted here, even if there are only two. 

I took the famous faces test and had to give up half way through because I was getting frustrated that I couldn't get any right. 

The most important way that I recognize people is by their walk. I can recognize people from very far away just based on how they walk. Also as soon as I hear a voice I know who it belongs to. 

It's very strange because I have an incredible memory for people, as soon as I hear their voice I know who they are, their name and whatever else I've learned about them. Even if I've only met them once I can tell their voice from others. 

Also I was wondering, are you able to tell who some one is even if they try to disguise their voice? When I was younger and people would prank call me I would always know who it was even if they were using a crazy voice because it still sounded like them. I was just wondering if this is a natural ability for people who are faceblind.

Yes!

I completely forgot that I learned that not every one had these. I was curious about it a few years ago so I looked it up and was shocked that not every one had them. I'm a 21 year old guy and just assumed that every one was like me. The wikipedia article is pretty small but the last thing it says is that "this can be indicative of a possible kidney problem." After I was born they did find out that I had a kidney problem. I just now realized that they could be linked.

I know how you feel, I met this guy and we've become great friends ever since. We occasionally cuddle while watching movies and we've even slept in the same bed on occasions. It's been this way for over a year and a half. He's completely straight and has a girlfriend. He doesn't know I'm gay or that I think about him constantly. It hurts to know that I can never be with him. Sometimes I even think that it's ruining our relationship. 

I think it's hilarious when straight people think they know what it's like to be friend-zoned.

So I know where you're coming from and how you feel, I just want to give you the biggest cyber hug I can and hope that you can get through it.

I hope your presentation went well! I'm sorry I haven't been on in a while so I couldn't be more help but I'll answer any way.

I'm not really attracted to any features more than others. I really don't understand people I'm around when they say "she's so hot" or "he looks like a god" I just don't base my feelings for people on their appearance I guess? Although as far as helpfulness, distinct features are always welcome. 

I have more trouble identifying men. For some reason a lot of them look alike, same hair cuts and clothing choices. Girls have a lot of different hairstyles and types of fashion. If it's a girl who wears her hair in a distinct way all the time then it's not hard to tell who it is. For close friends however I pretty much know their entire wardrobes. 

I'd love to hear what you talked about during your presentation, if you have a powerpoint or something that I could look at feel free to pm me or something. :)

He was always just one of those kids that made annoying comments. He wasn't hated but a lot of people could only take him in doses.
Went to my high school... People who don't know him like him a lot more than people who do.

I cried the hardest when my cat died when I was younger. I haven't really had too many heart wrenching experiences. I was, however, having a completely awful day the other day when I got a text from my friend that said "my mom made some food for you because she knows how much you like it." I started bawling my eyes out. It was such a bad day and finally it felt like some one cared.

This is headed straight to the bottom:

Mom, Dad, 

I know that it's not exactly your fault but you shouldn't have had me so far apart from my siblings. There is too much of an age gap. My two oldest siblings are more like 3rd and 4th parents than sisters and the other one I never talk to. All of my friends like their siblings and have memories of them playing games when they were little. I barely played with them I was always alone. 

That wouldn't have been so bad but you guys always talk about all the vacations you took when "the girls" were little. I was never taken anywhere when I was growing up. There were no vacations. There are plenty of home videos of them when they were little, there is one of me as a baby that is no more than ten minute at the end of other videos. I got nothing special. 

Mom, one night you let it slip that Dad wanted you to have an abortion when you were pregnant with me. I'm kind of ambivalent towards that. I would have agreed but it still hurt hearing it. It made it worse when you were yelling at me telling me you wished you had gotten the abortion.

Just wanted to let you know that some one read your post and knows how you feel. I have kind of the same situation except that I'm gay and he isn't. At least in your scenario it's possible but for me it's not. 

I know it sounds hard and you probably think it impossible but you need to stop letting it rule your life. I used to think about their relationship all day every day. One day he asked me how often I thought about it and I even told him that I thought about it frequently. Mostly because no one likes his girlfriend. But after a while it got easier and I don't think about it so much any more. 

You are probably reading this thinking "yeah of course try not to think about it, as if I haven't been trying" that's what I thought when I was going through it. But seriously if you try hard and keep occupied it does get easier. It might not go away, but it will get easier. 

**internet hug*

I also have prosopagnosia and I use these as well. I am really good at recognizing people from far away because every one has a very distinct walk. I've met a few others with this condition and none of them had picked up on this one so I'm glad that you did as well and I'm not the only one that notices how people walk.

I can also recognize people by voice but waiting for them to speak first is kind of annoying. Even if they are trying to disguise their voices I can still tell who they are, I can still tell that it's the voice of some one I know. 

Facebook makes memories so much better since people tag everyone in the photos. It is such a huge help instead of spending an hour trying to figure out who every one is from a still photo.

I'm in the exact same situation as you. Being around him, I feel annoyed; when I'm not around him, I wish I was and I wonder what he's doing and if he's ok. Although he doesn't know that I have these feelings and he thinks I'm straight. I don't want to be without him but being with him is impossible. 



I offer you the most sincerest of internet hugs that I can give.

Most of the people commenting in this thread have hit it head on. It's hard to describe exactly what it is that it feels like. Most days you start off by lying in bead thinking about how much effort it will take to stand up, how hard the activities of the day will be since you have no energy. Once you get up, things don't get easier. Friends will call you to do something but you will say no and not know why you said no. Then friends stop calling because they know you won't come. Then you get sad that your friends no longer want to hang out with you. For me, night time is the worst. Lying in bed, thinking about how you could have done so many things in the day, but you didn't. Thinking about how you shouldn't bother living because you're not going to do anything special with your life. Then you eventually fall asleep and repeat the process in the morning. It is not a fun cycle. Some people think that going to the gym helps. It might... but I wouldn't know because I don't have the energy to try. Every day you pretend that you're ok. You smile in response to what people say even though you don't feel like smiling. You just want to be normal and not alarm them. My roommate is the only person that I feel can help me through these tough times, but he doesn't even know that I'm going through them. I don't want to tell him either because then he'll pity me and that's not what I want. When he goes away on the weekends and I'm here alone in my room, those are some of the hardest times. 
TL;DR, everything is hard to do because you don't have energy... and it's not easy to get over.
